Supply chain reports indicate that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models have now entered mass production, gearing up for a September launch.

Assembly partner Foxconn is reportedly offering generous bonuses to returning workers in a bid to push recruitment numbers to their peak...

Reported by The Standard.

Citing supply chain sources, mainland media reported that Apple's major contract manufacturer Foxconn has entered its peak hiring season, with production capacity continuing to expand as the iPhone 18 series goes into mass production. The report indicated that the hourly wage at Foxconn's Zhengzhou Airport Zone A Business Group currently reaches as high as 27 yuan RMB (approximately HK$31.24), with rehired workers eligible for bonuses of up to 7,500 yuan RMB.

iPhone assembly is a seasonal process, so Foxconn and other Apple manufacturing partners need to hire large numbers of seasonal workers. Typically, they offer higher than usual hourly wages and use generous one-time bonuses to attract labour from rural areas of China to work in Zhengzhou.

Workers generally stay in company-provided dormitories for the duration of their contracts, which typically last around three months. Since the pay is far higher than what can be earned locally, the positions attract a considerable number of applicants.

Besides a more powerful chip and display upgrades, the upcoming flagship model is reportedly set to make three controversial trade-offs. Sources suggest the new device will be thicker and heavier than its predecessor, and will continue the unpopular design first introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro of offering no black or dark grey colour options.
